It takes a lot of self-awareness to recognize that pattern in yourself. Feeling like you go from zero to a hundred can be incredibly exhausting and overwhelming, especially when the reaction feels automatic and out of your control. 

When you feel that sudden surge of anger, the most powerful tool you have is creating a tiny gap between the trigger and your reaction. Try practicing a "stop and step back" technique: the moment you notice that familiar heat rising, physically step away from the situation and take three deep, slow breaths. This brief pause can help reset your nervous system, giving your logical brain a chance to catch up with your emotions before you react. If this explosive anger continues to interfere with your daily life or relationships, speaking with a counselor or therapist could be a great way to explore the root causes and learn personalized strategies to defuse that ticking feeling.
